subject: Re: Structured commitment proposal — earnout reserve and staged payments
messages:
From: Will O'Connor <will@nimbus.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-year commitment idea + payment flexibility

Hannah / Marissa —

Thanks for the demo last week. Nimbus is ready to move from pilots to a production commitment, but procurement and our finance team are pushing for flexibility on payment cadence. High level ask: a 3-year commitment with a large prepay component (we can do 40–60% upfront) but we need the remaining balance on extended terms (Net60/90 depending on taxes).

Two things we care about:
- We want a mechanism where if our usage materially exceeds committed units in year 1 or 2, we receive a credit (to be used against future invoices or as a refund) — call it an "earnout credit".
- We prefer staged invoicing tied to ramp milestones (so we can align rev recognition and budget approvals).

Can Redwood propose a clean structure that balances your discount tiers with our procurement constraints? Happy to provide our draft PO/term sheet — attaching a short internal note.

Thanks,
Will
Will O'Connor
Head of Cloud Ops, Nimbus Analytics
will@nimbus.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: Nimbus-Request-Terms.pdf (pdf)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Will O'Connor <will@nimbus.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@nimbus.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-year commitment idea + payment flexibility

Will / Priya —

Appreciate the clear asks — excited to get Nimbus into prod. Below is a commercial structure that should be straightforward to operationalize and address finance/procurement concerns. High level proposal (we can tweak):

Option A (Preferred for best pricing):
- 3-year commitment, 50% prepay at signature (applies to Year 1 commitment).
- Years 2–3: quarterly milestone invoices (25% of remaining committed spend per quarter) invoiced Net60.
- Earnout credit: up to 15% of annual committed spend reserved as an "earnout pool". If usage > committed units in a year, credits are applied to the next invoice or refundable at end of Year 3 (mutually agreed metric).
- Early-pay credit: 4% credit applied if Nimbus elects to prepay Years 2–3 in full at signature.

Option B (mix for procurement):
- 40% upfront, 20% at 12 months, remainder monthly billing Net60.
- Earnout handled as monthly reconciliation with a capped reserve (10% of upfront held as reserve, released quarterly).

Key tradeoffs to be mindful of:
- Larger upfront improves discount and gives you predictability; Redwood needs clarity for revenue recognition (finance request).
- Net90 is doable only for a limited portion (e.g., milestone invoices) and requires explicit SOW language and internal finance approval.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to run the commercial concessions sheet and confirm margin impact.
2) Ben to validate finance recognition and any escrow/reserve constraints.
3) If agreed, I will produce a one-page Mutual Action Plan and a revised SOW.

Attaching a quick pricing workbook (draft) and SOW stub. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to align with your procurement and tax teams.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com | +1 510-555-0199

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Nimbus commercial — suggested negotiation playbook (internal)

Team —

Quick internal note after Will's ask and my reply. Primary objectives: close a 3-year ARR-backed commitment with predictable unit economics while protecting margin and avoiding open-ended Net90 exposure. Suggested positions to defend/offer:

Our asks (must-haves):
- Limit Net90 to a fixed % of committed spend (max 20%), otherwise Net60.
- Earnout credit capped (<=15%) and applied as credit first, refund only at EOY3 if unused.
- Require clear ramp milestones and measurable unit definitions in SOW (API qps, token ceilings).

Concessions we can make:
- Add an early-pay credit (3–5%) if they prepay Year 2/3 in full.
- Offer a staged escrow/reserve model where 10% of upfront is held and released quarterly.
- Slightly higher discount ladder for 3-year vs 1-year (10%/12%/15% across years).

Ops asks:
- Ben: confirm whether we can support 20% Net90 exposure from revenue recognition and collections POV.
- Dev: confirm any technical holdbacks for ramp-based milestones (how we'll measure overage).

Marissa: can you draft the MAP and proposed concession table? I'll take the SOW language for the earnout pool and credit application.

Thanks — Hannah
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Nimbus commercial — suggested negotiation playbook (internal)

Hannah —

I like the framing. A few concrete tweaks I recommend we propose back to Nimbus:

1) Payment structure I will propose to the customer:
- 30% upfront at signature
- 20% placed in an "earnout reserve" (escrowed against contract performance, released quarterly based on usage)
- Remaining 50% invoiced against milestones: 2x 25% milestone invoices (end of Q1, end of Q2) — invoiced Net60.

2) Earnout / Reserve mechanics:
- Reserve equals 10–20% of committed spend (we recommend 20% for initial negotiation).
- If actual usage > committed units, credits first consume reserve; if reserve insufficient, apply overage pricing then true-up at EOY.
- Any unused reserve at EOY3 converts to an account credit (not a cash refund) unless finance approves refund on request.

3) Discount ladder (commercial):
- Year 1: 10% off list
- Year 2: 12%
- Year 3: 15%
- Additional 2% credit if Nimbus pre-pays full term at signature (rather than staged).

4) Payment term ask:
- We can agree Net90 on one milestone invoice only (subject to finance approval). All other milestone invoices Net60.

Operational notes:
- Ben: please confirm whether the reserve as an "account credit" (vs cash refund) is a hard blocker for Nimbus finance. If they insist on cash refund, we should push back and request higher upfront or lower discount.
- Dev: we need definitions for "committed units" — propose token baselines per month and monthly usage reporting cadence for reconciliation.

I'll draft a 1-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and mark the concession points. Sharing to Will once we've aligned internally.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0177

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Structured commitment proposal — earnout reserve and staged payments

Hannah / Marissa —

Thanks — this is helpful and closer to what procurement needs. Two quick asks before we proceed to legal/PO: 

- Can we shorten the milestone invoice Net90 to Net60 for both milestone invoices? Our treasury prefers Net60 across the board, and Net90 causes internal approval delays.
- Can you produce the one-page MAP you mentioned with the reserve mechanics spelled out (who holds the reserve, release cadence, reconciliation windows)? If you can also include the SOW snippet that defines "committed units" (monthly token ceilings and reporting cadence) that will accelerate internal sign-off.

We'll return our security questionnaire (attached) and confirm whether finance will accept account credit vs cash refund. Team — attaching our security questionnaire for your SOC/infosec review.

If you can send the MAP and SOW snippet, we can aim to route to legal this week. We like the discount ladder and earnout reserve approach — appreciate the flexibility.

Best,
Will
Will O'Connor
Head of Cloud Ops, Nimbus Analytics

Attachment: security-questionnaire.pdf (pdf)
